new:
- A PREMISE A CURE TAKES OUT OF THE COUNT LEAVES `counted_premises` TOO (ASK 638 part A; Shared Library, the cure result and cureRewrite): the cure result carries, per side, the premises that CURED items took out of the count (cpDrop): each CURED K-UNX, K-UNX-A, K-UNX range or E-ASM item whose reason reads "takes the premise out of the count". The send-back result carries none. Before the array is brought in line with the count, cureRewrite drops those premises from that side's `counted_premises` only when all of these hold: the count before the cure minus the count after equals the number of premises dropped; every dropped premise is in the array; no premise is both added and dropped; the array then has the count's length; the count after is not 0. It then writes "[AUDIT v50: COUNTED PREMISES DERIVED (pkgCPD) -- SEAT: <seat>; SIDE: <side>; COUNT: <a> to <b>; WAS: [..]; NOW: [..]; FROM: the cure took premise(s) <list> out of the count; record-only, it removes no seat ; END]". When any condition fails nothing is dropped and the array is derived as before. The count, every cure outcome and the send-back path are unchanged. Two things a judge can be sent follow the corrected array: the enforcer prompt's line "STORED COUNTED PREMISES FOR THIS SIDE: ...", which marks a dropped premise "not counted (SPARED)"; and the gate's D38 BASIS check, which runs only on a side whose array length equals its count, so it can raise a LIVE gate item on a side the cure lowered, and such an item left uncured counts in drv_uncured. The K-G8 check runs before the cure, on the array the judge wrote, and is unchanged. Not shown by a run. Mark for the first run in which a cure lowers a count by K-UNX or E-ASM: the stored array's length equals the count, and an AUDIT v50 DERIVED line names the premise taken out.
